chunks: Abu Mansur Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Bakr al-Khuri in Naysabur narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Khuri narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Faqih al-Khuri narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Juyibari, who is also called al-Hirawi, al-Niharawani, and al-Shaybani, narrated from al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him)
He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The reward for one upon whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has bestowed monotheism is nothing but Paradise.'

key_terms.التَّوْحِيدِ: Monotheism (the belief in the oneness of God)
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic (an honorific for God)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for monotheism according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, this hadith from Imam al-Rida traces the chain of authority back to the Prophet, affirming that Tawhid is not merely a theological concept but the definitive criterion for divine reward. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the purity of monotheistic belief as the essential gateway to Paradise, distinguishing it from mere ritual observance. This narration reinforces the theological principle that true faith, rooted in the recognition of God's oneness, guarantees eternal bliss.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 17. Abu Mansur Ahmed ibn Ibrahim ibn Bakr al-Khuri said in Naysabur, that Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammadibn Harun al-Khuri said: Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Faqih al-Khuri said: Ahmad ibn `Abd Allah al-Juyibari known as al-Hirawi, and al-Niharawani and al-Shaybani said on the authority of al-Rida `Ali ibn Musa, on the authority of his father on the authority of his forefathers on the authority of `Ali (AS)
that the Messenger of Allah (sw) said: “The reward for one upon whom Allah the Great and Almighty has blessed with monotheism is nothing but paradise.”
